title: Adequacy, nominal consideration, and sham exchange
shortTitle: Adequacy, nominal consideration, and sham exchange
summary: The legal sufficiency of an exchange differs from whether its values are equal.
notes: The notes place Restatement § 79’s treatment of adequacy alongside the requirement of a genuine exchange under § 71. A token amount may be part of an actual bargain, but a recital masking a gift creates a distinct question. The first and second Restatements’ examples illustrate that the formal presence of a dollar is not a complete analysis. Public-gift restrictions discussed by the editors raise additional constitutional questions that ordinary consideration doctrine alone does not resolve.
